name: resume-hooks-silently-lost
description: Per-pane resume hooks go missing without any error — registration accepts a pane that doesn't resolve and writes a degenerate key, and valid entries are orphaned when a pane's window/pane coordinates change — so panes come back from a reboot with no resume.

bank.summary: Every other per-session tmux op carries the same colon blind spot; only ShowEnvironment is now classified.
bank.detail: wrapSessionTargetErr is wired into ShowEnvironment alone (internal/tmux/tmux.go:590) because that is the one the capture loop classifies against. HasSession (tmux.go:88,97), KillSession (tmux.go:258), SwitchClient (tmux.go:276), SetSessionEnvironment (tmux.go:774), ListClients (internal/tmux/clients.go:19) and SaverPanePIDOrAbsent (internal/tmux/saver_pane_pid.go:13,37) all compose exactTarget and will report a live colon-named session as absent, indistinguishably from a real one. Routing them through the same wrapper is a single mechanical pass, but it changes error classification for callers across cmd, internal/restore and internal/spawn.

bank.summary: Two independent definitions of "a colon may not appear in a session name" now exist.
bank.detail: internal/session/naming.go:21 strips : (and .) at generation time via its own strings.NewReplacer, with no reference to the target grammar; tmux.ValidateSessionName (internal/tmux/errors.go) is the new recognition side. They agree today by coincidence, not by construction — the same generation/recognition drift the pane-token work consolidated into internal/nanoid. Deriving the generator sanitiser from the client predicate would close it, but the internal/session to internal/tmux import direction and the . case (a coord separator, not a session one) need deciding first.

bank.summary: A session name beginning with $ is unaddressable by name at all and still routes to natural churn — the same silent loss, a different character.
bank.detail: Measured on tmux 3.7c, isolated -S socket, with $foo as the only session: both show-environment -t "$foo" and -t "=$foo" fail with no such session (tmux reads a leading $ as a session-ID prefix). Unlike the colon this is NOT a regression from the exact-target change — the bare form fails identically — but the end state is the one this work unit exists to remove: tmux.ValidateSessionName returns nil for it, so wrapSessionTargetErr falls through to wrapNoSuchSession and capture.go logs a vanished session and drops a live one. internal/session/naming.go:20 already sanitises a wider set than the new predicate (periods and colons), so the repo holds two disagreeing definitions of an unwritable name. Also measured: . alone is fine (a.b resolves bare and exact), so a period is not itself a target-grammar break.

bank.summary: The prefix-sibling route enumeration omits both saver reads — the omission is why this defect survived to Phase 7.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/exact_session_target_realtmux_test.go:89 (TestSessionTargets_GoneSessionDoesNotReachPrefixSibling) and :189 (TestSessionTargets_LiveSessionStillResolves) enumerate eight per-session routes and neither lists SaverPanePID nor SaverPaneID. Folding the two saver routes into that suite — or deriving the case list from the set of per-session reads — makes the next per-session route guarded by construction instead of by a later analysis pass. The new saver_pane_pid_realtmux_test.go is a second, parallel expression of the same guard.

bank.summary: Three near-identical isolated-server seed helpers now exist in the package's real-tmux tests.
bank.detail: seedSaverServer (saver_pane_pid_realtmux_test.go:21), seedPrefixSiblingServer (exact_session_target_realtmux_test.go:41) and seedHookKeyServer (hookkey_realtmux_shared_test.go:19) each run the same SkipIfNoTmux, tmuxtest.New, EnsureServer, NewSession, WaitForSession sequence, differing only in socket prefix and topology; livePanePID and sessionPaneIDs are a matching near-duplicate pair. Rule of three is reached, and hookkey_realtmux_shared_test.go already exists as the package shared-fixture home.

bank.summary: The saver's own respawn addresses tmux by a bare session name — same defect class, one file over, and it carries -k.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/portal_saver.go:300 calls c.RespawnPane(PortalSaverName, portalSaverDaemonCommand), and RespawnPane (tmux.go:674) passes the target straight to respawn-pane -k -t <target>, which tmux parses as a pane target with no = pin, so it prefix-matches. Not exploitable as written — the call is inside the if createdSession branch, so _portal-saver was just created and exact-matches first — but the guard is ordering, not addressing, and the failure mode would be killing and respawning a prefix sibling pane with the daemon command. PaneTargetExact/exactCoordTarget would make it structural.

bank.summary: Real-tmux prefix-sibling coverage now lives in two files with two near-identical seed helpers.
bank.detail: seedSaverServer (internal/tmux/saver_pane_pid_realtmux_test.go:21-41) duplicates the SkipIfNoTmux, tmuxtest.New, EnsureServer, EvalSymlinks(t.TempDir()), NewSession, wait boilerplate of seedPrefixSiblingServer (internal/tmux/exact_session_target_realtmux_test.go:41-66, produced by task 6-7). The two files also assert the same invariant class — a gone session must not reach the live prefix sibling — under two different fixtures. Either fold the saver reads into 6-7 test pair (its goneSession/prefixSibling fixture works unchanged for an arbitrary session name), or extract the shared seeding into one helper both files call. Genuine tension: source-file-derived test naming argues for keeping a saver_pane_pid_realtmux_test.go, so extraction may be the better half of the trade.

bank.summary: tmuxtest.WaitForSession prefix-matches, so it returns on a sibling — every fixture staging a prefix sibling gets a readiness guard that does nothing.
bank.detail: internal/tmuxtest/socket.go:110 polls has-session -t name with no = prefix. Measured: with only _portal-saver-old live, has-session -t _portal-saver exits 0. Switching the helper to "="+name closes it for all consumers at once, but touches shared scaffolding used well beyond this task. This is the same prefix-matching defect the task itself fixes, one layer down in the test scaffolding.

bank.summary: ActivePaneCurrentPath doc promises a sentinel the route cannot produce, and its wrap is dead.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/tmux.go:246-248 states a session killed mid-read surfaces as errors.Is(err, ErrNoSuchSession). Measured: display-message -p -t "=gone:" -F "#{pane_current_path}" answers empty at exit 0, so wrapNoSuchSession(err) at :252 never fires and the promise is unreachable. Task 6-7 own test already records the truth (exact_session_target_realtmux_test.go:99-101), so the doc and its test contradict each other. Remedy (correct the doc, drop the dead wrap) lands in 6-7 output.

bank.summary: Two different classifiers guard the same hazard on per-session ops.
bank.detail: ShowEnvironment (internal/tmux/tmux.go:593) classifies through 7-1 wrapSessionTargetErr, which gates on ValidateSessionName first; saverPanePID (internal/tmux/saver_pane_pid.go:15) classifies through the bare wrapNoSuchSession. Unreachable today — every production caller passes the PortalSaverName constant — but SaverPaneID is exported with a free-form sessionName string, and exactCoordTarget("a:b") composes =a:b:, which tmux parses as session a. Deciding which per-session ops carry the unaddressable-name gate is 7-1 territory.

bank.summary: tmuxtest.WaitForSession waits on a prefix-matching target, so it is inert for any fixture that stages a prefix sibling; this task now carries a local duplicate of the exact-form poll.
bank.detail: internal/tmuxtest/socket.go:112 polls has-session -t <name> without the = exact prefix. Measured: with only _portal-saver-old live, that exits 0 for _portal-saver. Every fixture in the repo that seeds a sibling before the session under test silently loses its settle-window guard. Fixing it means editing shared scaffolding consumed across packages, which is why this task carries a local waitForExactSession in internal/tmux/saver_pane_pid_realtmux_test.go — the two should collapse into one exact-form helper.

bank.summary: ActivePaneCurrentPath documents a sentinel its route cannot produce — same defect class, one function away.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/tmux.go:246-248 claims a session killed mid-read surfaces as errors.Is(err, ErrNoSuchSession). Measured on 3.7c: display-message -p -t "=gone:" -F "#{pane_current_path}" exits 0 with empty output, so no error — and therefore no sentinel — is ever produced for a vanished session. Behaviour is still correct because internal/session/dirresolve.go:41-43 handles the empty string, but the contract on the exported method is a lie, and its wrapNoSuchSession call at tmux.go:252 is dead for the case it names. The fix lands in a different function with a different consumer (the TUI grouped render).

bank.summary: The package guard for this exact defect class omits SaverPaneID — the one method that just exhibited it.
bank.detail: TestSessionTargetsAreComposedExactly (internal/tmux/exact_session_target_test.go:32-102) enumerates seven *Client methods and their required target form but does not include SaverPaneID. The argv is pinned twice elsewhere (portal_saver_lifecycle_events_test.go:37, saver_pane_pid_test.go:27), so a regression is still caught; the central table simply under-claims. A one-row addition would make it complete.

bank.summary: saverPanePID classifies through the raw wrapNoSuchSession rather than 7-1 wrapSessionTargetErr, leaving a latent unreachable hole.
bank.detail: internal/tmux/saver_pane_pid.go:15. Every live caller passes the _portal-saver constant, so nothing can hit it today — but SaverPanePIDOrAbsent is exported with a free sessionName, and a colon-bearing name would make tmux answer can't find session: <first component> for a session that is alive, which the widened predicate now collapses to absent. Swapping in wrapSessionTargetErr(sessionName, err) is a one-identifier change that closes the latent hole and makes the two tasks machinery uniform.
